title: Fasting
hook: a small weekly fast keeps the heart free
tomorrow: first paycheck: how much of it is actually yours?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Samuel, Eli, and the line a guide, someone who helps you hear. Today the guide is your own stomach.

Fasting apps chart your eating window, time your hours and celebrate your streak. There the point is the body. So why would anyone choose to stay a little hungry for God? Jesus gives fasting instructions too, and the first one is a surprise: wash your face. In the Douay-Rheims: "But thou, when thou fastest anoint thy head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not to men to fast." No streak. No one's supposed to notice at all.
screen: `THE APP COUNTS YOUR HOURS.` → `WHY STAY HUNGRY FOR GOD?` → `WASH THY FACE.`

segments.voice: Notice the word Jesus uses: when, not if. He assumes his listeners will fast. And he moves it out of sight, so the only one who sees is the Father who sees in secret. Here's why it works on the heart. Hunger is a sense that keeps talking. The growl at eleven. The smell from someone's kitchen. The bag of chips in the cabinet that suddenly matters. Catholics use that voice as a reminder: each pang is a small nudge to pray, and proof that a person is more than an appetite. A small, steady fast loosens the grip of wanting, so the heart is a little freer to choose. Then the prophet Isaiah turns it outward. God asks: "Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen?" And the answer that follows is to deal thy bread to the hungry. The snack you skip can become someone else's meal. One to tell a friend: Church law names every Friday of the year a day of penance, not only in Lent, and lets bishops decide what that penance looks like where they are. A rule for life picks one small fast and keeps it weekly.
screen: `WHEN, NOT IF.` · `EACH PANG, A NUDGE TO PRAY.` · `DEAL THY BREAD TO THE HUNGRY.` · `EVERY FRIDAY, A PENANCE.` · then, large: `A LITTLE HUNGER.`

segments.voice: Pour a glass of water, or just picture one. Take one slow sip and follow it all the way down: cold, plain, enough. Then choose your weekly fast, small enough to keep, like a Friday snack or a second coffee, and picture who that bread could go to.
Fasting. A small hunger, kept quiet, that turns into prayer and into bread for someone else.
The line to keep: a little hunger, a face washed, a heart a bit freer. Day 1740, done.
